corresponding_K_past: K^+ = I^+ at every point (BTZ included), J^-(S); the E0 bundle is not time-symmetric (R4), so the past side is the core applied to the dual with Sing = ∅, not the dual of the future statement

findings: ETT.tex:2115: 'In particular I^-(p) is empty if and only if I^-(q) is' does not follow from the bijection I^-(p) ∩ J^+(Σ1) -> I^-(q) ∩ J^+(Σ2) alone: it also needs I^-(q) ∩ J^+(Σ2) ≠ ∅ for regular q, which is lem:Sigma_separe (J^+(Σ2) a neighbourhood of q ∉ Σ2) plus q ∈ Z^- — an unstated use of lem:Sigma_separe (image_Kminus_subset, case p BTZ / q regular).

ETT.tex:2133-2135: 'the sequence (j2(a_n)) is increasing and bounded above by q in M2, which is globally hyperbolic, so it converges' is asserted without proof; a cluster point in the compact J^+(Σ2) ∩ J^-(q) suffices and removes the need for the increasing sequence (rem:suite_croissante) altogether.

ETT.tex:2148-2156 (editorial proof of cor:ext_continue, '[editorial] supplied 2026-08-22 -- verify'): it uses cor:model_corresponding (stated after it, l.2158; first half only, so not circular) and lem:corresponding_K, which assume p ∈ J^+(Σ1) and the accumulation point q'' ∈ J^+(Σ2) — the statement of cor:ext_continue assumes neither (a point of J^-(Σ1) needs the K^+ form); and 'it eventually lies in a compact diamond of M2 by lem:image_diamant' (l.2155-2156) is unsupported: the x_m -> p are not shown to lie below one point of j1(N). Proved here instead from A3 (Sbierski Lemma 3.8).

ETT.tex:2159 / 2164: cor:model_corresponding's first assertion is stated for every p ∈ ∂j1(N), but its proof goes through lem:corresponding_K, which needs p ∈ J^+(Σ1) and both q, q' ∈ J^+(Σ2) (Sbierski footnote 21 handles the mixed case). Proved here in full generality from A3 (CGHDData.eq_of_corresponds); the K^- route gives it on the J^+ side only (IsCorrPair.eq_of_corresponds).

via A3 (Geometry.germExt_future / germExt_past, both time directions; p ∈ J^+(S) ∪ J^-(S) by mem_Jplus_union_Jminus_of_isCauchySurface from A2 curvesExtend). No lem:Sigma_separe needed. Partial because it rests on A3, an interface axiom gx discharges

hypotheses.paper: cone angle a local invariant (second assertion)
hypotheses.note: Geometry.isMor_sing applied to A3's extension phi (phi p = q)

any filter: (iii)=>(i) for any NeBot filter (model-free), (i)=>(ii) for every γ -> p within U (via A3). Timelike curves cannot be used at BTZ points (I^-(p) = ∅), hence the K^- form lem:corresponding_K

∃ W : Opens M, C = W ∩ ∂U; proof: A3's extension phi is continuous on O, so phi p' corresponds to every p' ∈ O ∩ ∂U. The second half of Lemma 3.8 (psi extends to U ∪ C) needs A1 to glue germs on overlaps: package 6

kb_proposals: x ∈ K⁻(p) gives J⁺(x) ∈ 𝓝 p (first countable, Jplus_mem_nhds_of_mem_Kminus); with causal convexity of U, lem:passe_pgcd for an open set is six lines (Kminus_inter_Jplus_subset_of_causallyConvexIn) — no image_diamant, no splitting.

A statement symmetric in (M, U, ψ) and (N, V, ψ⁻¹): bundle the pair (IsCorrPair with .symm and .dual), prove one inclusion, get the other from .symm; the E₀ time asymmetry then enters only through the instantiation of the K-calculus bundle (KSide C S sing₀ in the future, KSide C.dual S ∅ in the past).

Opens coerced to a type (↥U) is not syntactically ↥(U : Set M): `rw [Gluing.C_eq_closure U.isOpen.isOpenEmbedding_subtypeVal …]` fails; state the equation as a `have` at the Opens-typed form and rewrite with it.

lem:Sigma_separe without a splitting: S acausal + M = J^+(S) ∪ J^-(S) + K^- density + compact J^-(S) ∩ J^+(x) (T2) give J^-(S) closed, hence J^+(S) ⊇ M ∖ J^-(S) ∋ y for y ∈ J^+(S)∖S (Causality.Jplus_mem_nhds_of_isAcausal); the past twin is the same lemma for C.dual.
